description: Figure 13 is labelled as a three-panel comparison of spinodal decomposition versus cellular transformation after tempering at 800 °C, but only one panel — the one containing panel (a), the 9Al-10Mn-1C grade — is present in the supplied image. It is a single electron micrograph; the annotation burned into the image reads "20kV X2,500 10µm", i.e. 20 kV accelerating voltage, ×2,500 magnification, with a 10 µm scale bar at bottom-left. The field is strongly bipartite. The upper third is a dark, continuous band of coarse elongated colonies from which vertically oriented elongate rods/lamellae grow downward into the field. Below this front lies a much lighter matrix showing fine, dense, mottled or modulated contrast — the spinodal-type decomposition product — with a few small dark pores or etch pits. In the bottom-right corner an irregular dark block with sharp internal boundaries interrupts this pattern. No composition, phase-fraction or size values are printed on the panel; the alloy label, the 800 °C tempering treatment and the claim that cellular and spinodal products coexist come from the caption, and the claim that cellular products dominate in 9Al-10Mn-1C comes from the citing text.

subfigures.description: Electron micrograph of 9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C, annotated "20kV X2,500 10µm" (20 kV, ×2,500 magnification, 10 µm scale bar bottom-left). A dark upper band of coarse elongated colonies sends vertically oriented elongated rods downward into a lighter, finely mottled matrix; a few small dark pores/etch pits and an irregular dark block at bottom-right are visible.

observations.observation: The supplied image is a single electron micrograph bearing the in-image annotation "20kV X2,500 10µm" (20 kV accelerating voltage, ×2,500 magnification, 10 µm scale bar).

The microstructure is bipartite: a dark band of coarse elongated colonies occupies the upper part of the field, from which vertically oriented elongate rods/lamellae extend downward into a lighter matrix.
The lower/central lighter region shows a fine, dense mottled (modulated) contrast, plus a few small dark pores or etch pits.
An irregular dark block with sharp internal boundaries occupies the bottom-right corner of the field.
No numeric composition, phase fraction, hardness or size values are printed anywhere on the panel.
The caption ties panel (a) to the alloy 9Al-10Mn-1C after tempering at 800 °C.
The caption lists three grades for this figure — (a) 9Al-10Mn-1C, (b) 12Al-20Mn-1C and (c) 12Al-30Mn-1C — all tempered at 800 °C, although only the panel (a) field is present in the supplied image.
The citing text states that in 9Al-10Mn-1C (Fig. 13(a)) cellular transformed fractions were predominant over spinodally decomposed ones because of lower Mn% stability.
The citing text states that in 12Al-30Mn-1C (Fig. 13(c)) only spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume.

The citing text reports that in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C some grains feature a mixed structure of ferrite branches (linked to + -carbide lamellar grains) extending inside spinodally decomposed grains (Fig. 14).
